In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Mulk

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion, and He is over all things competent.﴾

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has already explained the meaning of tabāraka (blessed/exalted), mentioned the views of the exegetes and their differences regarding its meaning. He preferred that, according to the lexical sense and derivation, it is of the form tafā'ul from al-barakah (blessing), and the meaning is: blessings and goodness have multiplied from Him. This entails His greatness and His sanctity. . etc.

Then he noted a point about its not being conjugated and its being restricted to Allah, may He be exalted, and the Arabs' use of it for Allah, may He be exalted.

He also said in his dictation: ﴿in whose hand is dominion﴾, i.e., the effective power of the One who has decree over everything, who disposes of everything as He wills, with none to repel His judgment. End of quote.

The placing of the relative pronoun and its clause here, with the attribute specific to Him, may He be exalted, namely His saying tabāraka, indicates the greatness of the relative (the One described).

This is supported by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So glorified is He in whose hand is the sovereignty of all things, and to Him you will be returned﴾ [Yā Sīn: 83]; for the prefacing with glorification (tasbīḥ), which is transcendence (tanzīh), is equivalent to the prefacing with His saying tabāraka, and the relative pronoun after the glorification with its clause is just like the relative pronoun after tabāraka with its clause, exactly alike. This confirms what the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, mentioned in his dictation. And Allah knows best.

The distinction between al-Malik (the King) and al-Mālik (the Owner) has already been indicated at His saying: ﴿the King, the Holy, the Peace, the Giver of security﴾ [al-Ḥashr: 23]. Here the two attributes are combined: the One in whose hand is dominion and the sovereignty of all things is the Owner who possesses dominion over it, and He is the Lord of the worlds, glory be to Him.

**The Word of Allah, Exalted:** ﴿Who created death and life that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾.

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has already explained the meaning of this noble verse, together with the verses that clarify it, in his discussion of the Lord's words ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 56], and earlier, in Surat Hud, in his discussion of the words ﴿that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾ [Hud: 7]. (p-228)

He, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his dictated lessons (imla'): He has made for the world two deaths and two lives, and He clarified this by His words: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were dead and He gave you life, then He causes you to die, then He gives you life again﴾ [al-Baqarah: 28], and the rest of the verse.

The verse indicates that death is an existential matter and not a mere non-existence, as the philosophers (al-Falasifa) claimed, because if it were non-existence, creation could not be related to it.

* *

**The Word of Allah, Exalted:** the verse.

The mention of the creation of the seven heavens in layers (tibaq), in this manner, without disparity or fissures, after the mention at the beginning of the surah, indicates that the creation of these seven is among the perfections of His power.

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has explained the wisdom behind the creation of the heavens and the earth in a reminder he included at the end of Surat al-Dhariyat.

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has already explained the meaning of this noble verse and the verses that clarify it, in his discussion of the beginning of Surat Qaf, at the Lord's words ﴿Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We built it and adorned it, and it has no fissures?﴾ [Qaf: 6]. In his dictated lessons he said: The words of Allah, ﴿in the creation of the Most Merciful﴾, are general, encompassing all His creatures, in terms of evenness, wisdom and precision in workmanship. The heavens are included in this, by the evidence of His words: ﴿The handiwork of Allah, who has perfected everything﴾ [al-Naml: 88]. The perfecting of everything is according to its nature, as in His words: ﴿Our Lord is He who gave everything its creation, then guided it﴾ [Ta-Ha: 50].

And His words: ﴿He who made good everything He created, and began the creation of man from clay﴾ [al-Sajdah: 7]. This condition of the sky applies only in this world. It will be split apart on the Day of Resurrection, as in His words: ﴿When the sky is split apart﴾ [al-Infitar: 1], ﴿When the sky is rent asunder﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 1], ﴿and the Day the sky will be split open with clouds﴾ [al-Furqan: 25], and similar verses.

**The Word of Allah, Exalted:** ﴿Then look again; do you see any fissures?﴾

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has already explained this in his discussion of the Lord's words ﴿And We made the sky a protected ceiling﴾ [al-Anbiya': 32] in Surat al-Anbiya', (p-229) and at His words ﴿Have they not looked at the sky above them﴾ [Qaf: 6] in Surat Qaf. Perhaps the coming of this verse after ﴿that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾ [al-Mulk: 2] is a directive to the excellence of Allah's workmanship and His originality in His creation: ﴿You see no disparity in the creation of the Most Merciful﴾ [al-Mulk: 3].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 67, verse 5:

The Almighty said: ﴿And We have certainly adorned the nearest heaven with lamps, and made them missiles against the devils, and prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze.﴾

Our Shaykh (may Allah have mercy on him and on us) has already given a full explanation of the adornment of the heaven with lamps and their being missiles against the devils, at the words of the Almighty: ﴿And We have certainly set in the heaven constellations and adorned it for the beholders, and guarded it from every accursed devil, except him who steals a hearing, and he is pursued by a clear flaming fire﴾ [al-Hijr: 16-18].

He also touched upon part of this discussion in surah "al-Furqan", and it is necessary to join it to this topic there, because some of these matters are linked to others.

A Caution

Those modern inventions have appeared, and the proponents of new theories have made their claims, and people are divided into two groups: a group that rushes to deny, and another that hastens to affirm, and each of the two parties may cite texts from the Qur'an or the Sunnah in support. Perhaps the better course is to say: modern theories are of two kinds. A theory that contradicts the explicit text of the Qur'an is rejected without dispute, such as the theory that the sun is stationary, given the Almighty's words: ﴿And the sun runs on to a resting place for it﴾ [Ya-Sin: 38].

And a theory that does not contradict the text of the Qur'an and on which the Qur'an gives no explicit ruling, and for which we have no means of knowledge that either supports it or rejects it. The better course for us is a stance of caution: we should not rush to a definite judgment, either affirming or denying, and this is taken from the story of the hoopoe and Sheba with the Prophet Sulayman, when it came and informed him, and he (peace be upon him) had no knowledge of them beforehand, so he neither denied the report on the ground that it came from the hoopoe, nor affirmed it, because he had not known of them previously, even though it described their condition with precise description.

His stance (peace be upon him) was a stance of caution, though he had at his disposal the means of discovery and verification from the wind, the birds and the jinn. So he said to the informant, who was the hoopoe: ﴿We shall see whether you have told the truth or you are of the liars﴾.

We in this age are not more capable than the Prophet Sulayman was at that time, and those who report on such theories are no less than the hoopoe. So let our stance at the least be the stance of one who will see whether the report is true or whether it is shown to be false. The purpose of this caution is that we should not burden the words of the Qur'an, in matters where it is not explicit, with what it cannot bear, and then it becomes clear that the theory is false or true; thus we place the Qur'an in the position of comparison with modern theories, while the Qur'an is above all that: ﴿Falsehood does not approach it from before it or from behind it; it is a revelation from One who is Wise and Praiseworthy﴾ [Fussilat: 42].

The Almighty said: ﴿Then return the gaze twice; the gaze will return to you humbled while it is fatigued﴾.

What is explicitly stated here is returning the gaze twice, but the reality of looking is four times.

The first is in His words: ﴿You will not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any discrepancy﴾ [al-Mulk: 3].

The second is in His words: ﴿Then return the gaze; do you see any fissure?﴾ [al-Mulk: 3].

The third and fourth are in His words: ﴿Then return the gaze twice﴾ [al-Mulk: 4].

There is no further emphasis beyond repeating the gaze four times. And "ḥasīr" means one who is weary, exhausted, incapable, cut off without reaching the goal, as in the words of the poet:

"Whoever extends his glance beyond its limit returns with his glance weakened and exhausted."

al-Qurtubi said: It is said "his sight has become exhausted (ḥasura baṣaruhu), it grows weary, ḥusūran," meaning it has become weary and its looking has ended from long distance, and whatever is similar to that is ḥasīr and also maḥsūr.

He said:

"I looked at her in al-Muhassab of Mina, and my glance returned to me while it was weary."

The Almighty said: ﴿And We have certainly adorned the nearest heaven﴾.

So "ad-dunyā" is the feminine of "adnā", meaning the heaven nearest to the earth. Its implication is that the remaining heavens do not contain the lamps which are the stars and planets, as He said: ﴿with the adornment of the planets﴾ [as-Saffat: 6]. This implication is supported by what was reported from Qatadah: that Allah made the stars for three purposes: two of them here, namely the adornment of the nearest heaven and missiles against the devils; and the third is signs and guidance on land and sea. These three matters relate to the nearest heaven, because the devils do not penetrate to the other heavens, since they are protected bodies, as in the hadith of the Night Journey: "It has gates which are knocked upon, and no one enters from them except with permission."

Likewise His words: ﴿Indeed, those who denied Our signs and were arrogant towards them, the gates of heaven will not be opened for them﴾ [al-A'raf: 40].

Likewise, there is no one who needs guidance by them in his journey, since the angels each have their place which Allah has assigned to them; and because the adornment will not be seen because of the existence of the body of the nearest heaven. Thus it is established that the stars are specific to the nearest heaven.

Allah has indicated this in His words: ﴿Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with the adornment of the planets﴾ ﴿and as a guard from every rebellious devil﴾ [as-Saffat: 6-7].

The implication of "ad-dunyā" is that it does not exist beyond it, and there is no devil outside the nearest heaven.

* *

The Almighty said: ﴿And We made them missiles against the devils﴾.

They are meteors of fire, and meteors are fire, as in His words: ﴿Or I will bring you a burning brand that you may warm yourselves﴾ [an-Naml: 7]. The missiles and meteors are those with which the devils are struck when they steal a hearing, as in His words: ﴿Whoever listens now will find for himself a watching flame﴾ [al-Jinn: 9].

And His words: ﴿Except one who snatches a fragment, so he is pursued by a piercing flame﴾ [as-Saffat: 10].

Here there is a question: if the jinn are from fire, as in His words: ﴿and He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire﴾ [ar-Rahman: 15], how does fire burn them?

Al-Fakhr al-Razi answered it by saying: some fire is stronger than other fire, and the stronger affects the weaker. What supports what he went to is His words following it: ﴿And We have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze﴾ [al-Mulk: 5], and "as-Sa'ir" is the most intense of fire.

It is known that fire has levels, some more intense than others, and this is a tangible matter: an implement may be made of iron and a stronger iron implement may be applied to it, and it breaks it.

As it is said: "Only iron blunts iron." Thus, that its origin is from fire does not prevent it from being punished by fire, just as the origin of man is from clay, from black mud moulded, and from dry clay like pottery; and after his creation he cannot bear punishment by dry clay or by pottery, for he may be finished by a single blow from a piece of pottery. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 67, verse 7:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When they are cast into it, they will hear from it a roaring while it boils up, almost bursting with rage﴾.

The Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon him and upon us) said in his dictation on this verse: It is an affirmation that the Fire has perception (ḥissan), awareness (idrakan) and will (irādah). The Qur'an affirms of the Fire that it becomes enraged, sees, speaks, and seeks more, as He said here: ﴿almost bursting with rage﴾ [al-Mulk: 8].

And He said: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its raging and its roaring﴾ [al-Furqan: 12].

And He said: ﴿The Day We will say to Hell, "Are you filled?" and it will say, "Are there any more?"﴾ [Qaf: 30].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 67, verse 8:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Every time a company is cast into it, its keepers will ask them﴾.

Allah the Exalted has made clear that the Fire has keepers (khazana). He has also made clear that these keepers are the angels assigned to the Fire, as in His saying: ﴿Over it are angels, stern and severe, who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and do what they are commanded﴾ [al-Tahrim: 6].

He also specified their number in His saying: ﴿Over it are nineteen﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 30].

And He said: ﴿We have not made the companions of the Fire except angels, and We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 31].

Our Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, said in his dictation: This verse indicates that the people of the Fire will enter it in group after group, as in His saying: ﴿Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister﴾ [al-Anfal: 38].

* *

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Did there not come to you a warner?﴾.

Our Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, said in his dictation: This is the question of the angels to the people of the Fire. "Nadhir" (warner) means "mundhir" (one who warns); it is a form of "fa'il" in the sense of "maf'il". Although it is reported from al-Asma'i that he denied this, its parallels in the Qur'an include: ﴿Originator (badi') of the heavens﴾ [al-Baqarah: 117], meaning "mubdi'" (originator), and "alim" [al-Baqarah: 10], meaning "mu'lim" (painful).

Among the speech of the Arabs is the verse of Amr ibn Ma'dikarib:

Does Rayhana, the summoner who listens (al-sami'), keep me awake while my companions sleep?

So "al-sami'" here means "al-musmi'" (one who makes to hear).

And the verse of Ghaylan:

And from the breasts of ... there rises a painful (alim) blaze that turns away their faces.

That is, "mu'lim" (painful). And "indhar" (warning) is informing combined with frightening.

He also said: This verse indicates that Allah the Exalted does not punish anyone with the Fire except after He has warned them in this world. This meaning has been extensively demonstrated with its proofs at His saying: ﴿And We would never punish until We send a messenger﴾ [al-Isra': 15], and he cited this verse there.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 67, verse 9:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They will say, "Yes, indeed. A warner had come to us"﴾.

They acknowledged the coming of the warner to them.

And Allah, exalted is He, clarified this in His saying: ﴿And there has been no nation but that a warner has passed among them﴾ [Fatir: 24].

The Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 67, verse 10:

God Almighty said: ﴿And they will say, "If only we had listened or reasoned, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze."﴾

The Shaykh, may God's mercy be upon us and upon him, said in his dictation: That is, the people of the Fire will say: ﴿If only we had listened﴾ to one who understands from God His proofs, ﴿or reasoned﴾ about God's proofs, ﴿we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze﴾, that is, the Fire. They did hear, but they did not hear what would benefit them in the Hereafter, and they did reason, but they did not reason about what would benefit them in the Hereafter. This is because God said: ﴿God has sealed their hearts and their hearing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 7].

And He said: ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness﴾ [al-Kahf: 57].

Several explicit texts clarify what he mentioned, may God's mercy be upon us and upon him. Among them is the basic fact of their complete creation, in His saying: ﴿Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixture that We may try him, and We made him hearing and seeing﴾ (p-234) [al-Insan: 2].

And at the end of this Surah, "Al-Mulk," is His saying: ﴿Say, "It is He who produced you and made for you hearing, sight, and hearts; little are you grateful"﴾ [al-Mulk: 23].

But they did hear and they disobeyed, as in His saying: ﴿They said, "We hear and we disobey," and they were made to drink in their hearts the calf because of their disbelief﴾ [al-Baqarah: 93].

And this, although it concerns the Children of Israel, He addressed to this Ummah: ﴿And do not be like those who said, "We hear," while they do not hear﴾ [al-Anfal: 21]. And He said about them: ﴿They say, "We have heard. If we willed, we could say the like of this"﴾ [al-Anfal: 21].

And He said about them: ﴿They say, "We have heard. If we willed, we could say the like of this"﴾ [al-Anfal: 31].

And His saying about them: ﴿And those who disbelieve said, "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it"﴾ [Fussilat: 26].

And God has explained the reason they do not benefit from what they hear, in His saying: ﴿Woe to every sinful liar who hears the verses of God recited to him, then persists arrogantly as though he had not heard them. So give him tidings of a painful punishment. And when he learns of some of Our verses, he takes them in ridicule﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 7–9].

And His saying: ﴿And when Our verses are recited to him, he turns away arrogantly as though he had not heard them﴾ [Luqman: 7].

So their saying here, ﴿If only we had listened or reasoned﴾, means: listening with understanding and comprehension.

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Dafa' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-420) In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Surah Al-Mulk.

God Almighty said: ﴿And they will say, "If only we had listened or reasoned, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze."﴾

The apparent meaning of this noble verse indicates that they did not hear or reason in the worldly life. But other verses indicate the opposite, such as His saying: ﴿And We made for them hearing and sight﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 26].

And His saying: ﴿He barred them from the way, though they were discerning﴾ [al-Ankabut: 38].

We have already presented the answer to this in detail in our discussion of His saying: ﴿deaf, dumb﴾ [al-Baqarah: 18], and of His saying: ﴿And if their fathers did not understand anything, nor were they guided?﴾ (the verse) [al-Baqarah: 170].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 67, verse 11:

His saying, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on us and on him: ﴿So they will confess their sin, and so away with the companions of the Blaze.﴾

He said, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on us and on him, in his dictation (imla'): "al-i'tiraf (confession) is al-iqrar (acknowledgement). That is: they acknowledged their sin on the Day of Resurrection, at a time when acknowledgement and remorse benefit nothing." He had previously, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on us and on him, explained at length the extent to which the disbelievers benefit from this acknowledgement, at His saying, the Exalted: ﴿On the Day when its interpretation comes, those who had forgotten it before will say, "The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth. So are there for us any intercessors to intercede for us, or could we be returned so that we might do other than what we used to do?"﴾ [Al-A'raf: 53].

He also drew evidence from this verse, the verse of "al-Mulk" (surah 67), there.

The apparent meaning is that the principle in all of this is that their confession and their faith after the time has passed, at the moment of direct witnessing (mu'aynah), (p-235) is as came concerning Pharaoh in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Until, when drowning overtook him, he said, "I believe that there is no deity except that in which the Children of Israel have believed, and I am of the Muslims."﴾ [Yunus: 90]. It was said to him: ﴿Now? And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters.﴾ [Yunus: 91].

And it came in the clearest form in His saying: ﴿On the Day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before or earned through its faith some good.﴾ [Al-An'am: 158].

So when some of the signs of Allah come and the truth becomes manifest, there is no place for faith after direct witnessing: ﴿no soul will benefit from its faith﴾, that is, faith from before the witnessing, as in the state of Pharaoh mentioned; because the reality of faith is affirmation of the unseen, and when one witnesses it, it is no longer unseen at that time, so the time of faith and knowledge with Allah passes. Upon this is the hadith on repentance: "as long as he has not yet been in the death rattle" (ma lam yughargir).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 67, verse 12:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen—for them is forgiveness and a great reward.﴾

Al-khashyah (fear coupled with awe) is intense fear, as Exalted is He said: ﴿Those who fear their Lord unseen, and they are apprehensive of the Hour﴾ [al-Anbiya' 49].

Exalted is He has explained the locus of this khashyah in His saying: ﴿Only those among His servants who have knowledge fear Allah﴾ [Fatir 28], because they know the right of Allah, Exalted is He, and they are mindful of Him.

Exalted is He has also explained the reality of the fear of Allah: ﴿And indeed, among stones are those from which rivers gush forth, and indeed, among them are those that split and water comes out of them, and indeed, among them are those that fall down out of fear of Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah 74].

And His saying: ﴿Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and split apart from fear of Allah﴾ [al-Hashr 21].

So those who fear their Lord unseen are those who know the right of Allah over them and His watchfulness over them, in private and in public, and who know that He observes them however much they hide and conceal themselves, and who are always turning back penitently to Allah, as in His saying: ﴿This is what you were promised, for every returning, keeping [to the covenant]; who feared the Most Merciful unseen and came with a penitent heart﴾ [Qaf 32–33]. This is the highest degree of conduct with Allah, Exalted is He, and He has explained that it is the station of the scholars.

Exalted is He has also censured those who hide from people and do not hide from Allah, and who fear people but do not fear Allah: ﴿So Allah has more right that you fear Him, if you are believers﴾ [al-Tawbah 13].

Singling out Allah alone for khashyah is the station of the prophets, as in His saying: ﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him and fear none except Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Reckoner﴾ [al-Ahzab 39].

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, said: The Arabs praise the one who is in his solitude as he is in his presence before people.

And from this is the saying of Muslim ibn al-Walid:

He avoids errors in his solitude, pure of heart; his unseen self is like his witnessed self.

The reality is that this attribute, namely the fear of Allah unseen and faith in the unseen, is the foundation of all of the Muslim's action and dealings, because by his faith in the unseen he will do every good deed seeking the reward of Allah, as at the beginning of the Mushaf: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. That is the Book about which there is no doubt, a guidance for the God-fearing, who believe in the unseen﴾ [al-Baqarah 1–3], and the verse continues.

And by fearing Allah unseen he will avoid every evil, so he will be safe, and there will be attained for him what Allah, Exalted is He, said about them: ﴿Forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [al-Ma'idah 9]: "forgiveness" for his sins, and "a great reward" for his deeds. May Allah grant us His khashyah in private and in public.

It should be known that what is meant by "the unseen" here is that which is on the side of the servant, not of his Master, as in the hadith on ihsan: "That you worship Allah as if you see Him; and if you do not see Him, then indeed He sees you," and this awareness is the strongest factor in acquiring the khashyah of Allah, glorified is He.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 67, verse 13:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And keep your speech secret or declare it; indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾

In this is an indication that secrecy and openness are equal before Allah and in His knowledge, because He is "Knowing of what is within the breasts" (ʿalīmun bi-dhāt al-ṣudūr), He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal.

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is the same whether any of you conceals his speech or openly declares it﴾ [al-Ra'd: 10].

And His saying: ﴿And if you speak aloud, indeed He knows the secret and what is more hidden﴾ [Ta-Ha: 7].

The Shaykh (al-Shinqiti) had already explained this verse under each of the two verses.

And His saying, may He be exalted, has already passed: ﴿Allah has heard the speech of the one who argues with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Mujadila: 1].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him﴾ [Qaf: 16].

And there has passed, in the surah "al-Tahrim," immediately before this surah, His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement, and when she informed [of it] and Allah disclosed it to him﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Tahrim: 3]. In it is a practical, observed demonstration that He, may He be exalted, knows the secret and what is more hidden. Therefore He, may He be exalted, said here:

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 67, verse 14:

﴿Should He not know, He who created? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.﴾

As He said in Surah "At-Tahrim": ﴿She said, "Who told you this?" He said, "I was informed by the All-Knowing, the All-Aware."﴾ [At-Tahrim: 3]

Al-Qurtubi said, quoting Abu Ishaq al-Isfara'ini: Among the names of the Essential Attributes (asma' sifat al-dhat) is that which pertains to knowledge, namely al-'Alim (the All-Knowing), and its meaning is the comprehension of all that is known. Among them is al-Khabir (the All-Aware), which is specific in that He knows what will be before it comes to be. Among them is al-Hakim (the All-Wise), which is specific in that He knows the subtlest of attributes. Among them is al-Shahid (the Witness), which is specific in that He knows the absent and the present, and its meaning is that nothing is hidden from Him. Among them is al-Hafiz (the Preserver), which is specific in that He does not forget. Among them is al-Muhsi (the Counter), which is specific in that the multitude does not distract Him from knowledge, such as the light of day, the intensity of the wind, and the falling of leaves; so at that moment He knows the parts of the movements in every leaf. And how could He not know, when He is the One who creates? He has said: ﴿Should He not know, He who created? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.﴾

Regarding ﴿man﴾ in His words ﴿Should He not know, He who created?﴾, they permitted that it be the subject of (ya'lamu, "knows"), which is Allah the Exalted; that is, He who created knows what He created, and He is the One who knows what is in the breasts.

They also permitted that it be the object, with the subject being a concealed pronoun within the verb (ya'lamu). Al-Qurtubi and Abu Hayyan both mention both possibilities, and it is clear and admissible.

However, what the texts support is that it is the object, as in His words: ﴿Indeed, He is All-Knowing of everything﴾ [Ash-Shura: 12], and ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal﴾ [Ghafir: 19].

And His words: ﴿And Allah created you and what you do﴾ [As-Saffat: 96]; and among their deeds is what they conceal and what they openly declare. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 67, verse 15:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is He who made the earth docile for you, so walk in its broad tracts and eat of His provision, and to Him is the resurrection.﴾

Dhalul (docile, subdued) is on the pattern fa'ul in the sense of maf'ul (object of the action), and it is an intensive form expressing subjugation. One says: a dhalul animal, clearly tame. Several statements have been made regarding the meaning of the earth being made subservient, and there is no contradiction among them. Their collective sense revolves around enabling benefit from it, along with facilitating stability upon it and securing it with mountains, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the mountains He set firmly, as an enjoyment for you and your livestock﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 32-33].

And from the possibility of cultivation in it, as in His saying: ﴿Then We made grain grow therein, and grapes and fodder﴾ [Abasa: 27-28], up to His saying again: ﴿as an enjoyment for you and your livestock﴾ [Abasa: 32]. Most of these meanings have been gathered in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle, for the living and the dead? And We placed therein firm mountains, high, and gave you to drink sweet water﴾ [al-Mursalat: 25-27].

I used to hear our Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, say concerning this verse: it is part of Allah's subjugation of the earth, that He made it a receptacle for man during his life, by facilitating his livelihood from it and his life upon its surface; and when he dies, it is also a receptacle for him by his burial in it.

He would say: Had Allah willed, He could have made it of iron and copper, so man could not plough in it, nor dig, nor build, and when he died he would find no grave in it.

Among what points to all these meanings is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So walk in its broad tracts and eat of His provision﴾ [al-Mulk: 15]; because it is connected to what precedes it by the particle fa' (so), i.e., because of its being made docile, by making walking in its regions easy, and seeking provision in its expanses through means within it, such as farming, craft and trade, etc.

The imperative in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So walk in its broad tracts and eat of His provision﴾ is for permissibility (ibahah). However, the placing of this command after His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is He who made the earth docile for you﴾ contains a favour from Allah, may He be exalted, upon His creation, which indicates that in this command, along with permissibility, there is direction and encouragement for the community to strive, work and exert itself, and to walk in every direction across the earth's broad tracts, in order to subdue and master it, which makes the community more entitled to it than others.

As He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Do you not see that Allah has subjected to you what is in the earth, and the ship that runs upon the sea by His command?﴾ [al-Hajj: 65].

(p-239) And in His saying: ﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, all of it from Him﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 13], and other verses.

Whoever sees this subjugation acknowledges Allah's bounty, stands in praise of Allah, and presents gratitude, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And the camels We have made for you as among the symbols of Allah; in them is good for you. So mention the name of Allah over them while they stand in rows; then when they fall on their sides, eat from them and feed the contented and the beggar. Thus We have subjected them to you that you may be grateful﴾ [al-Hajj: 36].

And His saying: ﴿And He who created all the pairs and made for you of the ships and livestock that which you ride, so that you may sit upon their backs, then remember the favour of your Lord when you are seated upon them, and say: Exalted is He who has subjected this to us, and we were not capable of it. And indeed, to our Lord we will surely return﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 12-14].

That is: along with thankfulness for the blessing, there is admonition, lesson, and inference of the perfection of power.

Among these meanings is the return and the going back to Allah, may He be exalted. So His saying: ﴿and to Him is the resurrection﴾ comes after walking in the broad tracts of the earth and seeking provision, and what this entails of reflection and contemplation on the causes of causes and Allah's subjugation of them, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed, to our Lord we will surely return﴾ after mention of: ﴿He created all the pairs﴾, i.e., the kinds, and the subjugation of ships, livestock, sea and land. In it there is implicitly the affirmation of the power to resurrect. Thus walking in the broad tracts of the earth, employing its expanses, exploiting its wealth and benefiting from its goods is not solely for seeking provision; otherwise, provision could be driven to them. Rather, it is for taking up the means first, for reflecting upon the effects, for drawing a lesson from created things, and for preparing provision for what follows death, as in the verse of "Friday" (al-Jumu'ah): ﴿Then disperse in the earth and seek of Allah's bounty, and remember Allah much that you may succeed﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 10].

That is: upon witnessing the signs of His power and the greatness of His favour.

On this basis, the Qur'an has placed the Islamic community in the most honourable positions of wealth, self-sufficiency, investment and production. Nothing of its worldly affairs has been lacking except in proportion to its shortcoming in carrying out this work and its squandering of its right in this existence.

Al-Nawawi said in the introduction to al-Majmu': the Islamic community must work to invest in and produce all its necessities, even the needle, so that it may be independent of others; otherwise it will need others in proportion to its shortfall in production. And this is the reality of the world today, since productive capacity is what dominates and holds international sovereignty.

Allah has granted the Islamic world priority in all of this. Therefore it must occupy its place, preserve its standing, and build its entity through both religion and worldly life together. And success is from Allah.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 67, verse 16:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Are you secure that He who is in the heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you, and suddenly it will shake?﴾

Abu Hayyan mentioned, regarding the reading of "ءَأمِنتُمْ" (a'amintum), several readings: realizing both hamzas (tahqiq), facilitating the second (tashil), inserting an alif between them, and other forms. Al-khasf (khasf, swallowing) is the earth's going down with them, as Qarun was swallowed up. Al-mawr (mawr, shaking) is agitated movement, or movement with speed. Allah, exalted is He, fixed it with mountains as pegs, as He said: ﴿And the mountains He set firm﴾ ﴿as a provision for you﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 32–33]. As for ﴿He who is in the heaven﴾, Ibn Jarir said: it is Allah, exalted is He. End of quotation.

Al-Qurtubi attributed it to Ibn Abbas. What supports what he said is what follows it of the earth's being swallowed and the sending of the violent wind (al-hasib), for none can do that except Allah. It is also the apparent meaning of the text. With this, al-Kisa'i's view, and that of those who followed him such as Abu Hayyan, is refuted, when they said that it is on the basis of an omitted element, a kind of metaphor (majaz). Their metaphor, in their view, is that His dominion (malakut) is in the heaven, i.e., by omitting a modifier (hadhf mudaf), and His dominion is in everything; but the heaven was singled out for mention because it is the dwelling place of His angels, and there is His might, His Kursi, and the Preserved Tablet, and from it His decrees, books, commands and prohibitions descend, etc.

It was also said: it is Jibril, because he is the one entrusted with the swallowing. And it was said: it is a concession to them in their belief that Allah is in the heaven. These sayings are based on denying the attribute of elevation (uluw) to Allah, exalted is He, and fleeing from what they regard as anthropomorphism (tashbih). But what the salaf adhered to is contrary to what they went to, and the creed of the salaf is exactly what Ibn Jarir said, based on the hadith of the slave-girl: "Where is Allah?" She said: "In the heaven." He said: "Free her, for she is a believer." And on the basis of several verses with this meaning.

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, examined this topic in the broadest and clearest manner possible, leaving no ambiguity and no doubt, and no Muslim, whether scholar or student, can do without it. The scholar takes from it the sound method of teaching and the wise style of exposition, and the student takes from it what is obligatory upon him of (p-241) a upright, clear, evident and sound creed.

It may be said that the meaning of (fi) is enclosure (zarfiyyah), so we make the heaven a container for Allah, exalted is He. This would imply likening Him to something that occupies space (mutahayyiz).

It is said in reply: He, glory be to Him, is transcendent above enclosure in the known sense that is established for created beings.

The texts of the Sunnah have indicated the negation of this regarding Him, exalted is He, and its impossibility rationally for Him, glory be to Him, in the hadith: "The seven heavens within the Kursi are nothing but like a ring or dirhams thrown into a shield, and the Kursi within the Throne is nothing but like a ring thrown into a desert, and the Throne in the hand of the Merciful is nothing but like a mustard seed in the hand of one of you." Thus the enclosure of the heaven for Him, glory be to Him, in the sense known to us, is negated; and because He, glory be to Him, is established upon His Throne.

In what the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, presented in this topic there is healing and sufficiency, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace. Al-Qurtubi said: "(In the heaven)" means above the heaven, like His saying: ﴿So travel through the earth﴾ [al-Tawbah: 2], i.e., above it, not by contact or enclosure.

It was also said: (fi) means "upon", like His saying: ﴿And I will crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees﴾ [Ta-Ha: 71], i.e., upon them... and the reports on this subject are numerous, authentic, widespread, and indicative of elevation; none rejects them except a heretic, an ignoramus, or an obstinate person, and their purpose is to exalt Him and to declare Him far above the lowest and the bottom, and to describe Him with elevation. End of quotation.

What he mentioned is precisely the doctrine of the salaf, although he mentioned words whose ending contains ta'wil and whose ending contains tanzih.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 67, verse 19:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not considered the birds above them, spreading their wings and folding them in? None holds them up except the Most Merciful. Indeed, He is Seeing of all things.﴾

"Birds" (al-tayr) — "spreading their wings" (saffat): i.e., extending their wings. "Folding them in" (yaqbidna): i.e., drawing them in toward their bodies.

Abu Hayyan said: He coordinated the verb "yaqbidna" with the noun "saffat" and did not coordinate it with the noun "qabidat" (folding in), because the basic state in flight is the spreading of the wing, while folding is an occurrence that arises. What Abu Hayyan said accords with their established rule that the noun indicates permanence and stability, while the verb indicates renewal and occurrence. Thus the constant motion in flight is the spreading of the wings, and the new element added to it is the folding.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿None holds them up except the Most Merciful﴾ is a proof of His power, exalted is He, and a sign for His creation, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not considered the birds subjected in the atmosphere of the sky? None holds them up except Allah. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ [An-Nahl: 79].

So it is a sign of power. And it has come in other verses that He, exalted is He, is the One who holds the heavens and the earth by His power, majestic and exalted is He, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease; and if they should cease, no one could hold them after Him. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving﴾ [Fatir: 41].

So He, glorified is He, holds them both by His power, exalted is He, lest they cease. And if their cessation were hypothetically assumed, none could hold them but Him. Likewise in His saying: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah has subjected to you what is in the earth and the ship that runs upon the sea by His command, and He holds up the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission?﴾ [Al-Hajj: 65].

A reminder

Perhaps among the matters that call for attention is directing the gaze to the birds in the air (﴿spreading their wings and folding them in; none holds them up except the Most Merciful﴾), after the warning of the earth being swallowed up. The earth is suspended in the air just as the birds you see are suspended; none holds it up except Allah. The causing of the earth to be swallowed is like the dropping of the bird from the air, because all of them are held up by none but Allah, exalted is He, and He is capable of swallowing the earth and of dropping the bird.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 67, verse 21:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Who is it that provides for you if He withholds His provision?﴾

He, exalted is He, says to the polytheists: Who is it, other than Him, glorified is He, who provides for you if Allah withholds His provision from you?

The answer: No one is able to do that, and no one possesses it except Allah.

He, exalted is He, has explicitly stated this question and its answer in His statement: ﴿Say: Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth? Say: Allah﴾ [Saba': 24].

That is: there is none other than Him, glorified is He; there is no god but He. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? There is no god but He. Then how are you turned away?﴾ (p-243) [Fatir: 3].

This is because the One who has power over creation is the One who possesses the power over provision, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth, or who controls hearing and sight, and who brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living, and who arranges the affair? They will say, "Allah." So say, "Will you not then fear Him?"﴾ [Yunus: 31].

And like His statement: ﴿Allah is the One who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, then will bring you to life﴾ [Ar-Rum: 40].

This is from the perfection of power over giving life, causing death, and provision. He, exalted is He, has made clear that this belongs to the One in whose hand are the keys of all affairs, glorified is He, and the management of the affairs of creation, as in His statement: ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾, then He said: ﴿He extends provision to whom He wills and restricts [it]. Indeed, He is Knowing of all things﴾ [Ash-Shura: 12]. That is: He extends and restricts, He knows, not from deficiency or need, but He knows the interests of His servants. ﴿Allah is Subtle with His servants; He provides for whom He wills, and He is the Strong, the Mighty﴾ [Ash-Shura: 19]. That is: He deals with them with His subtle kindness, and He is Strong to provide for all with abundant provision, and He is Mighty in His dominion. So He extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it﴾ [Az-Zumar: 52]. That is: according to the requirement of subtle kindness and knowledge. ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that upon Allah is its provision﴾ [Hud: 6].

From all of this, a refutation is directed at those who seek provision from other than Him, as in His statement: ﴿And they worship other than Allah what does not possess for them any provision from the heavens and the earth at all, and they are not able﴾ [An-Nahl: 73].

He combined the two matters, reproof and guidance, in His statement: ﴿You only worship idols instead of Allah and you invent a falsehood. Indeed, those you worship other than Allah do not possess for you any provision. So seek provision from Allah, worship Him, and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 17].

He, exalted is He, has clarified the entire matter of creation, provision and worship in His statement: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want that they should feed Me. Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 56-58].

In the preceding verses He has clarified that He provides for the servants from the heavens and the earth in general.

(p-244) In other verses He clarified the manner of this provision in detail, which creation cannot accomplish, in His statement: ﴿Then let mankind look at his food. That We pour down water in torrents. Then We split the earth in splitting. And We cause to grow therein grain, and grapes and herbage, and olives and palm trees, and gardens dense with trees, and fruit and grass, as provision for you and for your grazing livestock﴾ [Abasa: 24-32].

So all kinds of provision in this begin with the sending down of water from the sky, then from it arises the splitting of the earth to bring forth plants of all kinds: grain, grapes, olives, palm trees, gardens and fruit, all of which are for mankind, while herbage and grass are for livestock. Livestock are also provision, in meat and milk. All of this is sustained by the sending down of water from the sky, and no one is able to do any of this except Allah.

So when Allah withholds it from creation, no created being is able to send it down. Therefore, when the Muslim knows that provisions are in the hand of the Creator, and that He in whose hand are the keys of the heavens and the earth, he will never turn with desire nor direct a request except to Allah, the Exalted, certain with the truest certainty that He, glorified is He, is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm.

As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And in the heaven is your provision and that which you are promised. So by the Lord of the heaven and the earth, indeed it is the truth, just as you speak﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 22-23].

It has been related from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, her saying: "By Allah, the faith of a servant is not perfected until his certainty in what is with Allah is greater than what is in his hand."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 67, verse 30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Tell me, if your water should become sunken, then who will bring you flowing water?﴾.

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has already explained this in his commentary on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We sent down water from the sky in a measured amount, and We caused it to settle in the earth, and indeed, We are able to take it away﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 18], in the surah "al-Mu'minun."
